producer_report.summary: A job now lands only on the branch it was dispatched from. Root cause: `land::plan` checked only that the job's base is an ancestor of HEAD and never compared branches. Dispatch now records the checked-out branch in a new optional `dispatch_branch` on `athena.job/1`. An empty value means a detached HEAD; an absent value means a record made before the field, which keeps the old behavior. `plan` takes a `Dispatched` argument, reads the current branch itself, and returns a new `Plan::OtherBranch(reason)` before the ancestor check. The reason names the dispatch branch. Retry after blocked (`retry_landing`) treats it like `Stale`: it bails and the job stays blocked, with nothing written. First landing (`land_or_block`) records a stale outcome only when the checked-out branch holds the job's `job.json`. Otherwise it bails and writes nothing. I confirmed the reason by disabling the rule: the gate then refused Athena's own commit because the closing score no longer followed from the branch's records. The dispatch branch then shows the job as `interrupted`. The land.rs header, CHANGELOG and tests are updated. Tests cover plan unit cases, records round-trips with and without the field, and three lifecycle tests through the real `go` flow. With the rule disabled, the three new lifecycle tests fail (Landed instead of Stale, a gate refusal, and a retry that lands). `cargo test --locked` exited 0, but I could not read the persisted output, so I have no per-test counts.

checks_run.note: The two new round-trip tests (with and without dispatch_branch, including the empty value) pass.
19 tests pass: the existing ones with `&Dispatched::Unknown` and the new branch-rule tests.

criteria_check.criterion: Run `cargo test`. A new test dispatches a job on branch A, switches to branch B (which contains the base commit), finishes the job, and shows that B's tip is unchanged and the outcome is stale (or blocked) with a reason naming the dispatch branch.
criteria_check.evidence: Two lifecycle tests: `a_job_finished_on_a_branch_with_its_records_goes_stale` and `a_job_finished_on_a_branch_without_its_records_changes_nothing` (run with `cargo test --locked -p athena-cli --test lifecycle a_job_finished_on_a_branch`), plus the land.rs unit test `a_job_dispatched_elsewhere_is_refused_on_another_branch`. With the rule disabled they fail. In the first test, `other` holds the job's records: state is Stale, the reason names `main`, `main`'s tip is unchanged, and `other` gains only `records/` paths. In the second, `other` lacks the job's records: `go` errors naming `main`, `other`'s tip is exactly unchanged, and nothing under `records/jobs/` exists on `other`. In the first case `other`'s tip gains one records-only commit rather than staying unchanged; see open_issues.

criteria_check.criterion: Run `cargo test`. A test shows a job still lands as a fast-forward when the checked-out branch at finish is the dispatch branch, including the records-only-changes replay case.
criteria_check.evidence: `a_candidate_lands_over_a_records_only_interleave` now also asserts that `dispatch_branch` is `main` and that the job landed on `main`. The land.rs unit test `a_job_lands_when_the_dispatch_branch_is_checked_out` covers head equal to the base and the replay after an excluded-path (`PRIVATE.md`) commit. It checks the merged tree keeps both the excluded file and the candidate's change. All pass.

criteria_check.criterion: Run `cargo test`. A test shows the retry-after-blocked landing path (close.rs ~484) also refuses when the current branch differs from the dispatch branch.
criteria_check.evidence: `a_blocked_job_will_not_retry_on_another_branch` blocks the job on `main`, checks out `other`, and calls `go`. It gets an error naming `main` and saying the job stays blocked; the tip is unchanged, there is no greeting and no `outcome-landed.json`. After checking out `main` again, `go` lands it. Without the rule the retry lands, so the error assertion fails.

criteria_check.criterion: Run `cargo clippy` and `cargo fmt --check`: both are clean, and the existing land and landing tests in crates/athena-core still pass.

A paragraph below it covers the empty-string detached case, a branch job finished on a detached HEAD, and jobs made before the field.

criteria_check.criterion: This change refuses more landings, and the higher refusal rate is intended: expected 5% of newly refused readings.
criteria_check.evidence: The extra refusals are shown by the new lifecycle and unit tests. The '5%' figure is an expectation about use, and no test or data in the repository measures it, so I did not claim to check it. `cargo test --locked` returned no error, so no existing same-branch landing test regressed.

open_issues: Criterion 1 wording versus behavior (the plan's open question, unanswered): when branch B holds the job's records, B's tip moves by one records-only stale commit and gains no job content. When B lacks them, B's tip is exactly unchanged but `go` ends in an error instead of a stale outcome. The cause is that the gate refuses a stale score commit on a branch without the job's records. Please confirm this reading.
Criterion 8's '5% of newly refused readings' is read as an expectation about use. No code or data measures it.

Edits outside the listed deliverables: crates/athena-core/src/run/mod.rs (the dispatch-time `Job` literal now sets `dispatch_branch` from `current_branch()?`, and the import gains `Dispatched`) and crates/athena-cli/tests/lifecycle.rs (the new integration tests). They were needed because dispatch is the only place the branch is known and only the `go` flow can show the behavior.

No existing test needed changing for the new rule; `plan` calls in the land.rs tests only gained `&Dispatched::Unknown`. No refusal-corpus case was added and docs/records.md was not edited, as the plan decided.
mistakes: I first wrote a nonsensical `show` closure in the replay unit test and a tautological ancestor assertion in the other-branch test. I rewrote both before running them.
learnings: Without `dispatch_branch`, a stale outcome committed on a branch that lacks the job's records is refused by the gate: the closing score and outcome totals do not follow from that branch's records. This was seen by running the new tests with the rule disabled, and it is the reason `land_or_block` bails instead of recording stale there.
`Git::run` does not trim its output, so use `.trim()` when comparing a `rev-parse` result.
The `during_verification` hook runs inside the verifier invocation, and the rest of `go` tolerates a checkout there. Both new branch-switch tests complete without unrelated failures.
`Job` struct literals exist only at run/mod.rs, store.rs and the records.rs test; every JSON stub omits the key and parses through `#[serde(default)]`.
desires: A way to read the persisted full-suite test output, since Grep and Read were denied outside the working directory. Per-test counts from the full run would have been useful.
